summary: Created opsbot on both node1 and node2 (password-locked accounts), generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed its public key in node2's opsbot authorized_keys, and added Match User opsbot blocks (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) to sshd_config.d on both nodes. Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH to opsbot@node2 with the key and run commands, and that password-only auth attempts are rejected on both nodes. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + health baselines, rebooted node1 then node2 one at a time, confirmed boot_id changed on each, and reverified opsbot account, SSH keys/authorized_keys, and cross-node key-based SSH access all survived both restarts.
actions_performed: Checked baseline: no opsbot user on either node, PasswordAuthentication already 'no' globally, Ubuntu 24.04 on both nodes
Created opsbot user (useradd -m) and locked its password (passwd -l) on node1 and node2
Generated ed25519 SSH keypair for opsbot on node1 (~/.ssh/id_ed25519)
Installed node1's opsbot public key into node2's /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys (chmod 700/600)
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-opsbot.conf with 'Match User opsbot: PasswordAuthentication no, PubkeyAuthentication yes, AuthenticationMethods publickey' on both nodes
Discovered sshd had never generated host keys (ssh.socket socket-activated, keys missing); ran ssh-keygen -A and created /run/sshd on both nodes to unblock sshd -t validation
Validated sshd config syntax (sshd -t) on both nodes
Verified opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 SSH key auth works and runs remote commands
Verified password-only SSH auth attempts for opsbot are rejected with 'Permission denied (publickey)' on both nodes
Captured pre-restart boot_id and opsbot/SSH health baseline on both nodes
Rebooted node1 (backgrounded sudo reboot so ack returned before disconnect), polled until back, confirmed boot_id changed, reverified opsbot account/keys and outbound SSH to node2
Rebooted node2 the same way, polled until back, confirmed boot_id changed, reverified opsbot account/authorized_keys and inbound SSH from node1
Post-restart re-verified the 99-opsbot.conf Match block persisted and password auth is still rejected on both nodes

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: useradd + passwd -l succeeded on both nodes; id opsbot shows uid=1000(opsbot)

evidence.requirement: opsbot has SSH key-based access from node1 to run commands as opsbot on node2
evidence.summary: Generated ed25519 key on node1, installed pubkey in node2 authorized_keys, then opsbot@node1 SSH'd to opsbot@10.100.68.11 and ran whoami/hostname returning 'opsbot'/'node2'

evidence.requirement: key-based authentication required for opsbot on both systems (password auth rejected)
evidence.summary: Match User opsbot block with AuthenticationMethods publickey deployed on both nodes; explicit password-preferred SSH attempt returns 'Permission denied (publickey)' from both node1 and node2

evidence.requirement: sshd config validity after adding opsbot Match block (including fixing missing host keys)
evidence.summary: Discovered missing host keys blocking sshd -t, generated them with ssh-keygen -A and created /run/sshd, then sshd -t passed cleanly (SSHD_CONFIG_OK) on both nodes

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id bdd5de93...; reboot ack returned before disconnect (stream closed); post-reboot boot_id changed to eee6b2ad...; opsbot account, SSH keys, and outbound SSH to node2 all confirmed working after restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id dfeb3b70...; reboot ack returned before disconnect; post-reboot boot_id changed to dc9b465e...; opsbot account and authorized_keys intact, and opsbot@node1 successfully SSH'd into node2 post-restart returning 'POST_NODE2_REBOOT_OK'

evidence.requirement: key-only enforcement persisted across both restarts
evidence.summary: Post-restart on both nodes: 99-opsbot.conf Match block still present, and a password-only SSH attempt to node2 still returns Permission denied (publickey)
